Article.ArticleTitle: Sporadic intradural extramedullary hemangioblastoma of the cauda equina: case report and literature review.

Abstract.AbstractText: The purpose of this case report is to present a rare finding of an intradural extramedullary hemangioblastoma of the cauda equina, with literature review. Spinal hemangioblastomas account for 1-5% of all spinal cord tumors. While spinal hemangioblastomas are rare, it is exceedingly rare to have a case of intradural extramedullary hemangioblastoma of the spine, especially in isolation without von-Hippel-Lindau syndrome. Only 20 previous cases have been reported.

An 82-year-old male presented with MRI evidence of an intradural mass at the L4 spinal level. Given the benign appearance on MRI and lack of radiculopathy, the decision was made to observe. Over the course of four years, the tumor enlarged and caused left lower extremity radicular pain. Posterior laminectomy and tumor excision was performed. Due to intimate involvement with multiple nerve roots, subtotal resection was performed. Immunohistopathological analysis revealed a highly vascular and cellular tumor, with findings consistent with intradural extramedullary hemangioblastoma. The patient ultimately underwent CyberKnife radiosurgery for residual tumor, with improvement in neurological symptoms. Two year follow-up studies have failed to show any tumor growth.

Literature review reveals this to be a rare diagnosis of cauda equina intradural extramedullary spinal hemangioblastoma. Furthermore, this was a sporadic case without associated von Hippel-Lindau syndrome. Only 20 previous cases have been reported. Immunohistopathological analysis was required to make the diagnosis. Radiosurgery appears to be useful in cases of residual tumor after subtotal tumor resection.
